scenario.name: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Mandiant & MITRE — Azure VM CustomScriptExtension & IMDS Managed Identity Token Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a cloud office tower where building managers can slide a remote work-order envelope through the central dispatch wall straight into any locked virtual room without knowing the room own password. Using hijacked cloud manager rights, an intruder slips a custom script envelope through the wall, makes the room built-in guest butler execute it with full master keys, and reaches into the room internal badge box to lift the room cloud identity pass and widen their reach across the estate. In this scenario (T1059, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Mandiant & MITRE, Azure VM CustomScriptExtension & IMDS Managed Identity Token Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: aRM Control-Plane, then guest Agent SYSTEM Child Process Execution, then local IMDS Managed Identity OAuth Token. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ARM Control-Plane, then Guest Agent SYSTEM Child Process Execution, then Local IMDS Managed Identity OAuth Token, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: ARM Control-Plane Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write Invocation
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059 - Command and Scripting Interpreter)
stages.description: Without needing any SSH key or Windows password for the target server, the intruder uses compromised Azure management permissions to push a Custom Script Extension order straight down from the cloud control plane. Holding RBAC permissions on the subscription or resource group, the actor dispatches an ARM PUT request to Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write (or runCommand/action), recorded in AzureActivity logs (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with ArmOperation=MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/VIRTUALMACHINES/EXTENSIONS/WRITE, ExtensionType=Microsoft.Compute.CustomScriptExtension, TargetVirtualMachine=prod-app-vm01 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue =~ "MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/VIRTUALMACHINES/EXTENSIONS/WRITE" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue =~ "MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/VIRTUALMACHINES/EXTENSIONS/WR so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1059 during "ARM Control-Plane Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write Invocation" , Holding RBAC permissions on the subscription or resource group, the actor dispatches an ARM PUT request to Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write , or runCommand/action, recorded in AzureActivity logs while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact az vm extension list --resource-group prod-rg --vm-name prod-app-vm01 runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , az vm extension list --resource-group prod-rg --vm-name prod-app-vm01 against AWS CloudTrail so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1059 during "ARM Control-Plane Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write Invocation" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ PUT /subscriptions/.../virtualMachines/prod-app-vm01/extensions/CustomScriptExtension / ⇠#1 ACK 200) from Node ① (#1 Compromised Azure Contributor Principal) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254) & Key Vault).

stages.title: Stage 2: Guest Agent (WaAppAgent.exe / walinuxagent) SYSTEM Child Process Execution
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1078.004 - Cloud Accounts)
stages.description: Inside the virtual server, the always-running official Azure guest butler dutifully opens the incoming work order and launches the attacker script under supreme operating-system authority, leaving an unmistakable parent-child tree on disk. Inside the guest OS, the Azure VM Agent (WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe or walinuxagent) downloads the extension payload into C:\Packages\Plugins\Microsoft.Compute.CustomScriptExtension\ (or /var/lib/waagent/custom-script/download/) and executes it as SYSTEM/root (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with ParentAgent=C:\WindowsAzure\Packages\WaAppAgent.exe, PluginDirectory=C:\Packages\Plugins\Microsoft.Compute.CustomScriptExtension\1.10.12\Downloads\0\, ExecutionIntegrity=NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe", "enable.cmd") (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any , "WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe" so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1078.004 during "Guest Agent , WaAppAgent.exe / walinuxagent SYSTEM Child Process Execution" , Inside the guest OS, the Azure VM Agent , WindowsAzureGuestAgent while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact ls -la /var/lib/waagent/custom-script/download/0/ runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ls -la /var/lib/waagent/custom-script/download/0/ via System / Runtime Execution Interface so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1078.004 during "Guest Agent , WaAppAgent.exe / walinuxagent SYSTEM Child Process Execution" , Inside the guest OS, the Azure VM Agent , WindowsAzureGuestAgent while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted -File C:\Packages\Plugins\Microsoft.Compute.CustomScriptExtension\1.10.12\Downloads\0\diag_collect.ps1 / ⇠#2 ACK 1) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Azure Resource Manager (ARM API)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254) & Key Vault).

stages.title: Stage 3: Local IMDS (169.254.169.254) Managed Identity OAuth Token Acquisition & Key Vault Read
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552.005 - Cloud Instance Metadata API)
stages.description: Standing inside the server with supreme local rights, the script taps the room local identity window (supplying the required Metadata header) to withdraw the server own Managed Identity cloud pass and immediately unlocks connected Key Vaults and storage accounts. Running inside the VM, the script queries http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01&resource=https://vault.azure.net with header Metadata: true to obtain the VM System-Assigned Managed Identity token and read Azure Key Vault secrets (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with MetadataEndpoint=http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token, KeyVaultOperation=SecretGet , sql-conn-string, CallerIdentity=System-Assigned Managed Identity , prod-app-vm01 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs | where ServicePrincipalName == "prod-app-vm01" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs | where ServicePrincipalName == "prod-app-vm01" via System / Ru so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.005 during "Local IMDS , 169.254.169.254 Managed Identity OAuth Token Acquisition & Key Vault Read" , Running inside the VM, the script queries http://169 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact AzureDiagnostics | where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT" and OperationName == "SecretGet" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , AzureDiagnostics | where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT" and OperationName == "Secr so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.005 during "Local IMDS , 169.254.169.254 Managed Identity OAuth Token Acquisition & Key Vault Read" , Running inside the VM, the script queries http://169 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ GET https://prod-fin-kv.vault.azure.net/secrets/sql-conn-string?api-version=7.4 / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 Azure Resource Manager (ARM API)) to Node ④ (#4 Azure VM WaAppAgent / CustomScriptExtension), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254) & Key Vault).
